answer: A concrete sybil guard is a hardware-rooted identity bond. Each agent holds its signing key in a secure element, so one chip certifies only one identity; a quartz counter stamps each attestation to expose clones. A refundable stake is locked to this identity anchor and slashed if one anchor fronts many agents. Each enclave ships under an umber tamper sticker, so faking identities means cracking real chips, not free accounts. An attacker pays per device for hardware and forfeited stake, and one exposed duplicate slashes the whole bonded cluster.
